Description: Life as a woodcutter in the old castle was not easy, yet it carried a quiet pride.
Before dawn, I would step into the forest, mist curling around the trunks of ancient trees.
The weight of my axe was familiar in my hands, each strike echoing through the woods like a heartbeat.
The smell of pine and earth filled my lungs, and the rhythm of chopping became the rhythm of my days.
Winter brought snow and biting cold, but the fire in the castle hearths and a warm meal kept me going.
Each log I cut fed the kitchens and warmed the halls, a small but vital part of life in the castle.
Though the work was hard, and danger sometimes lurked in the shadows, there was honor in sustaining the people within those stone walls.
I was but a woodcutter, yet my arms and my labor became the unseen lifeblood of the castle.
